text:
Maria L.: quick thread — we should discuss unifying the console query plumbing and the authz sidecar path. currently payloads go query-gateway -> console -> sidecar (sync) then back. duplicate serialization + extra network hop is adding ~10-25ms under normal load and spikes p99 under load.
Alex K.: do you have numbers for p50/p95/p99?
Maria L.: from last week's perf trace: p50 +6ms, p95 +14ms, p99 +28-35ms when authz cache miss rate hits 20%. end-to-end also shows extra CPU from serializing jwt/context twice.
Jamal R.: oof. are we sure it's just serialization? could be connection churn or TLS overhead too.
Maria L.: it's a combo. sidecar does helpful caching but it's a separate process so we lose in-proc cache and suffer grpc -> http translation in some paths.
Priya S.: caution: sidecar is our current security boundary for private deploys. moving authz in-process changes attack surface and memory isolation assumptions. we need threat model + KMS implications if tokens live in app memory.
Alex K.: tradeoffs: 1) keep sidecar and optimize (connection pooling, wire format) 2) expose authz lib (in-process) 3) hybrid: in-proc cache + fallback to sidecar.
Maria L.: thinking hybrid is safest: in-proc adapter that does quick cache lookup and returns an opaque allow/deny + handle; on cache miss we forward to sidecar. minimizes coupling and preserves fallback.
Jamal R.: that sounds good. rollout idea: implement adapter with same semantics as sidecar, add feature flag to switch routing at gateway for canary tenants. fallback by default to sidecar if adapter errors.
Priya S.: also add strict audit logging: adapter must forward an audit record to the control plane (or sidecar) for any decision that wasn't purely cache-hit. otherwise we lose traceability.
Alex K.: interface sketch:```\n// authz adapter interface\nCheck(ctx, token, resource) -> { decision: allow|deny, reason: string, cache_key?: string }\n// on cache miss -> proxy to sidecar with same request id\n```
Maria L.: + also return a short-lived proof handle so downstream services can avoid rechecking repeatedly for the same request. handle validity aligned with cache TTL.
Jamal R.: perf-wise this will give us p95 ~ baseline + 2-4ms (in-proc path) and p99 bounded by sidecar proxy when misses. much better than current p99 tail.
Priya S.: requirements: (a) threat model doc (b) memory handling for tokens (c) audit hook (d) canary plan (e) tests for cross-tenant leak.
Alex K.: operational: we need metrics broken out by path: adapter-hit/miss, sidecar-proxy-rate, decision-latency, audit-forward-latency. add these to console dashboard.
Maria L.: rollout plan proposal: 1) implement adapter + unit tests (2 weeks) 2) add gateway flag + dashboard metrics (1 week) 3) canary 10% tenants -> 50% over 2 weeks -> monitor p99/authorization errors (2 weeks) 4) kill old path when stable.
Jamal R.: fallback behavior must be: on any adapter failure -> return an explicit error to gateway to force sidecar route, not allow-by-default. safer.
Priya S.: agreed. also schedule a short security review during the canary.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy created for team/console-authz-adapter (build 2221). :rocket:
Maria L.: action items: Maria (adapter proto + perf baseline), Alex (metrics + dashboard), Jamal (rollout automation + safe fallback), Priya (threat model + security review). I'll open RFC PR with the interface sketch and perf numbers today. if no objections I'll merge RFC draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
Alex K.: no objections from me. let's make sure we have alerting on audit-forward latency > 200ms.
Jamal R.: will add runbook note for adapter fallback and sidecar surge.
Priya S.: adding security review meeting for tomorrow 10:30.
Maria L.: thanks all — will post RFC link soon.
